prompt: At a college, $60$ percent of students own a tablet, $50$ percent own a gaming console, and $30$ percent own both. What is the probability that a randomly chosen student owns a tablet OR a console?
hint: Some students own both devices. If you add the two percentages, how many times are those students counted?

hints.text: Some students own both devices. If you add the two percentages, how many times are those students counted?
Use the general addition rule $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$, which removes the double-counted overlap: $0.6 + 0.5 - 0.3$.
$0.6 + 0.5 - 0.3 = 0.8$, so the probability of owning a tablet or a console is $0.8$.

explanation: Adding $0.6 + 0.5 = 1.1$ counts the $30$ percent who own both devices twice, which is why the sum exceeds $1$.
Subtracting the overlap once fixes the double count: $1.1 - 0.3 = 0.8$.
So $P(\text{tablet or console}) = 0.8$, meaning $80$ percent of students own at least one of the two.
